help.Audio@@Audio Channel Layout: Sets the sound format the emulator sends to your speakers or headphones. Use 'Auto' to let the emulator pick the best format for your audio device and the game's audio.
help.Audio@@Audio Format: Switches the game's sound between stereo and surround. The automatic setting lets the game choose from all formats, the manual setting uses the ones you select, and changes need a game restart.
help.Audio@@Audio Provider: Chooses which PS3 audio system the emulator uses. Games use CellAudio, and only the PS3 system menu (VSH) needs RSXAudio.
help.Audio@@Convert to 16 bit: Uses 16-bit audio samples instead of the default 32-bit floating point. Try it if you get no sound or completely broken sound.
help.Audio@@Dump to file: Saves all game audio to a raw wave file. If unsure, leave this off.
help.Audio@@Enable Buffering: Buffers audio to reduce crackling and stutter, at the cost of a longer sound delay.
help.Audio@@Enable Time Stretching: Stretches audio to reduce crackling and stutter even more. It needs buffering turned on, and on slower devices it can make the sound noticeably worse.
help.Audio@@Microphone Type: Use Standard for most games. Choose SingStar for SingStar games, Real SingStar only with a real SingStar device, and Rocksmith with a Rocksmith dongle.
help.Audio@@Music Handler: Used only when a game plays music through the PS3 music player (cellMusic). Qt plays it through the device's default audio output, but may not handle every audio format.
help.Audio@@RSXAudio Avport: Chooses which PS3 audio output port (avport) the sound is taken from.
help.Core@@Accurate Cache Line Stores: Handles the PPU's cache line clearing instruction (DCBZ) accurately. With Accurate SPU DMA also on, SPU cache line writes are handled atomically too.
help.Core@@Accurate PPU 128-byte Reservation: Makes PPU atomic operations work on the whole cache line instead of a single 64-bit block. The number sets which operation lengths use the accurate version.
help.Core@@Accurate RSX reservation access: Pauses the RSX graphics chip during the SPU's GETLLAR and PUTLLUC memory reservation operations.
help.Core@@Debug Console Mode: Gives games more system memory, as on a PS3 debug console (DECR). Some games behave differently than on a retail PS3 with this on.
help.Core@@Disable SPU GETLLAR Spin Optimizat: Turns off an SPU waiting optimization. Only a few games need this, and it can cause severe slowdowns and stutter in many others.
help.Core@@Enable Performance Report: Measures certain events and prints a chart when emulation stops. Don't turn it on unless asked to.
help.Core@@Hook static functions: Replaces some game functions, such as 'memcpy', with the emulator's own versions. This is experimental and may do nothing or break things.
help.Core@@LLVM Precompilation: Compiles the game's extra PPU and SPU modules while it boots. When off, they compile as needed, which can interrupt gameplay often, so only turn it off to reach the game sooner.
help.Core@@MFC Debug: Writes MFC logs. Only useful to developers, so never turn it on.
help.Core@@Max LLVM Compile Threads: Limits how many threads compile a game's PPU and SPU modules the first time. The default uses all available threads; lower it to leave more for other apps.
help.Core@@Max SPURS Threads: Limits the SPURS threads in each thread group. It may help on devices with few CPU cores, but lowering it is likely to cause crashes, so keep the default.
help.Core@@PPU Accurate Non-Java Mode: Respects the PPU's Non-Java mode bit in vector math. If unsure, leave this setting alone.
help.Core@@PPU Accurate Vector NaN Values: Produces exact NaN (not a number) results in PPU vector math. If unsure, leave this setting alone.
help.Core@@PPU Debug: Writes PPU logs. Only useful to developers, so never turn it on.
help.Core@@PPU Reservation Priority Over SPUs: Gives the PPU an advantage while SPUs use memory reservations. It helps only a few games and can slow others down, so use it only when advised to.
help.Core@@PPU Set FPCC Bits: Sets the PPU's floating-point condition bits (FPCC) exactly. If unsure, leave this setting alone.
help.Core@@PPU Set Saturation Bit: Sets the PPU's saturation bit exactly. If unsure, leave this setting alone.
help.Core@@PPU Threads: Sets how many PPU threads can run at once. A value of 1 works with very few games, so leave it on the default of 2 if unsure.
help.Core@@Preferred SPU Threads: Limits how many SPU threads run certain timing-sensitive stages at once. A small value can reduce stutter in some games; leave it on auto if a small value makes things worse.
help.Core@@RSX FIFO Fetch Accuracy: "Atomic" greatly improves stability in many games at little speed cost. "Fast" is the least accurate, and "Atomic & Ordered" is the most accurate but slowest, with little extra stability.
help.Core@@SPU Block Size: Sets how large the compiled SPU code units are. Mega and Giga may run faster by joining small units together, while Safe gives the best compatibility.
help.Core@@SPU Debug: Writes SPU logs. Only useful to developers, so never turn it on.
help.Core@@SPU Profiler: Measures SPU performance while the game runs. Turn it on only when a developer asks, since it slows things down a little by itself.
help.Core@@SPU Reservation Busy Waiting Enabl: Makes SPUs spin while waiting for events (RdEventStat), which uses more CPU. It helps a few games on CPUs with 12 or more threads.
help.Core@@SPU XFloat Accuracy: Controls how accurately SPU float math is handled. It fixes bugs in various games at a speed cost, and applies only when SPU Decoder is set to Dynamic or LLVM.
help.Core@@SPU loop detection: Detects loops in SPU code and uses them as scheduling hints, which improves speed and lowers CPU use. In rare cases it causes severe audio stutter.
help.Core@@Set DAZ and FTZ: Flushes very small float values to zero (DAZ and FTZ), which speeds up the PPU at the cost of accuracy.
help.Core@@Sleep Timers Accuracy: Changes how precisely game sleep timers wait. 'As Host' uses the system's normal accuracy, 'All Timers' tries to improve it, and 'Usleep Only' improves only usleep calls.
help.Input/Output@@Background input enabled: Keeps controller and keyboard input working while the emulator is not the app in focus.
help.Input/Output@@Buzz emulated controller: Emulates Buzz controllers. Select 1 or 2 controllers if the game needs them and you have no real ones, or Null if the game supports DualShock or you have real Buzz controllers.
help.Input/Output@@Camera: Select Qt to use the camera on your iPhone or iPad.
help.Input/Output@@Camera flip: Flips the camera image horizontally, vertically or both.
help.Input/Output@@Camera type: Some games need a specific camera type selected here.
help.Input/Output@@GHLtar emulated controller: Emulates Guitar Hero Live guitars. Select 1 or 2 controllers if the game needs them and you have no real ones, or Null if it supports DualShock. Real guitars also work alongside emulated ones.
help.Input/Output@@IO Debug overlay: Shows an overlay with player 1's controller input values. It appears only when the main debug overlay is off; if unsure, leave it off.
help.Input/Output@@Keep pads connected: Shows every configured controller as connected in the game, even when it is physically disconnected.
help.Input/Output@@Keyboard: Some games accept keyboard input, such as from a keyboard connected to your iPad. Basic works for these games.
help.Input/Output@@Lock overlay input to play: Lets only player one control the emulator's built-in on-screen menus.
help.Input/Output@@Mouse: Some games accept mouse input, such as from a mouse or trackpad connected to your iPad. Basic or Raw works for these games.
help.Input/Output@@Mouse Debug overlay: Shows an overlay with mouse input values. It appears only when the other debug overlays are off; if unsure, leave it off.
help.Input/Output@@Mouse-based gyro enabled: Turns on mouse motion control (gyro) when a game starts; a hotkey also toggles it. Hold the right mouse button and move for the X and Z axes, scroll for Y, and release to reset.
help.Input/Output@@Move: Emulates PlayStation Move. Fake is experimental and maps Move controls to your DualShock 3 mappings, while Mouse and Raw Mouse control it with a mouse.
help.Input/Output@@Pad handler mode: Single-threaded runs all controller handlers on one thread, and Multi-threaded gives each its own. Use Multi-threaded only if you can spare the extra threads.
help.Input/Output@@Show move cursor: Shows the raw position of the PlayStation Move input, which helps on calibration screens.
help.Input/Output@@Turntable emulated control: Emulates DJ Hero turntables. Select 1 or 2 controllers if the game needs them and you have no real ones, or Null if it supports DualShock. Real turntables also work alongside emulated ones.
help.Miscellaneous@@Automatically start games: Starts the game as soon as it has loaded. Leave this on unless you are a developer.
help.Miscellaneous@@Pause Emulation During Ho: Pauses emulation while the home menu is open. Most games pause themselves there, but this helps with the ones that do not.
help.Miscellaneous@@Play music during boot se: Plays the game's own music, if it has some, while the game boots.
help.Miscellaneous@@Prevent display sleep whi: Keeps the screen from turning off while a game is running.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show PPU compilation hint: Shows a 'Compiling PPU modules' message in the emulator's on-screen overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show RPCN popups: Shows pop-ups from your RPCN friend list.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show analog limiter toggl: Shows a message in the on-screen overlay when you toggle the analog limiter.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show autosave/autoload hi: Shows autosave and autoload messages in the on-screen overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show capture hints: Shows screenshot and recording messages in the on-screen overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show mouse and keyboard t: Shows a message in the on-screen overlay when you toggle mouse and keyboard input.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show pressure intensity t: Shows a message in the on-screen overlay when you toggle button pressure intensity.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show shader compilation h: Shows a 'Compiling shaders' message in the on-screen overlay.
help.Miscellaneous@@Show trophy popups: Shows a pop-up when you unlock a trophy.
help.Miscellaneous@@Silence All Logs: Stops writing logs once the game has started. Only use it if you believe it is necessary.
help.Miscellaneous@@Use native user interface: Uses the emulator's own in-game menus and dialogs, which work with game controllers. Its on-screen keyboard only has an English layout.
help.Miscellaneous@@Use recursive scan: Also looks in subfolders when scanning a folder for games. When off, only the chosen folder itself is scanned.
help.Net@@Clans Enabled: Connects to the Clans server. Only matters for games with the Clans feature.
help.Net@@Derive MAC from PSID: Builds the emulated console's network (MAC) address from its PSID, the console's ID.
help.Net@@Internet enabled: When set to Connected, games can use your internet connection.
help.Net@@PSN status: RPCN connects supported games to the RPCN server in place of PSN. Simulated fakes a PSN connection, but using PSN features may cause errors or crashes, and it is only in custom configurations.
help.Net@@UPNP Enabled: Turns on UPnP, which opens the game's network ports on your router automatically if the router has UPnP turned on.
help.Savestate@@Compatible Savestate Mode: Makes SPU emulation favor savestate compatibility, which may cost a little speed. When off, some games may refuse savestates and log an SPU pause error.
help.Savestate@@Start Paused: Loads savestates paused on the first frame, so you can get ready before the action starts.
help.Savestate@@Suspend Emulation Savestate M: Works like hibernation: saving quits the game, and a loaded savestate is hidden so it can't be reused to cheat. The file is ignored, not deleted, and can be relaunched by hand.
help.System@@Keyboard Type: Sets the keyboard layout the PS3 uses. Only US, Japanese and German layouts are fully supported.
help.System@@Language: Sets the PS3's system language. Some games fail to boot without it and others switch to it automatically, so pick a language the game supports.
help.System@@License Area: Sets the console region (license area) of the PS3. Some games may not work in every license area.
help.VFS@@Empty /dev_hdd0/tmp/: Clears the PS3's /dev_hdd0/tmp/ folder when a game boots. Some homebrew and game mods need this; if unsure, do not use this option.
help.VFS@@Emulate BD-ROM Read Speed: Slows disc reads to roughly a PS3 Blu-ray drive's speed. It may fix games that break when data loads too fast, such as corrupted videos, but loads take longer.
help.VFS@@Emulate HDD Read Speed: Slows data reads to PS3 hard drive speed. It may fix games that break when data loads too fast, but loading takes longer; if unsure, do not use this option.
help.VFS@@Enable /host_root/: Turns on the /host_root/ folder, which some homebrew needs. If unsure, do not use this option.
help.VFS@@Limit disk cache size: Deletes older files from the disk cache at boot once it grows past the size you set. Games keep only temporary data there, and this works only in the global settings.
help.Video@@3D Display Mode: Sets the stereo 3D mode, in custom configurations set to 720p only. Anaglyph suits color filter glasses, Side-by-Side suits most VR viewer apps, and Over-Under is closer to native.
help.Video@@Allow Host GPU Labels: Lets the GPU sync directly with the PS3 CPU, so the game sees the true state of GPU work. It can remove visual noise and glitches but costs speed, so use it with caution.
help.Video@@Anisotropic Filter Override: Higher values sharpen textures seen at an angle but use more GPU power. Keep it on Automatic to use the original PS3 setting.
help.Video@@Aspect ratio: Sets the shape of the picture. Leave it on 16:9 unless your screen is 4:3.
help.Video@@Debug output: Turns on Vulkan's built-in debugging, which slows games down badly. Only useful to developers; if unsure, leave it off.
help.Video@@Debug overlay: Shows an overlay with various debugging information. If unsure, leave it off.
help.Video@@Disable Asynchronous Memory Manag: Handles memory management calls right away instead of in the background. It can cause severe slowdowns and stutter, and only developers debugging texture cache problems need it.
help.Video@@Disable FIFO Reordering: Turns off all RSX command (FIFO) optimizations, so draws are processed in the order they arrive.
help.Video@@Disable Hardware Blending: Forces blending to be done in shaders (programmable blending) where supported. This is purely a debugging option, and turning it on gains you nothing.
help.Video@@Disable Hardware ColorSpace Remap: Stops using the GPU's own sRGB and SNORM texture formats. Turning it on is closer to the PS3, but the software emulation can add some visual noise.
help.Video@@Disable MSL Fast Math: Turns off fast math in the Metal shaders the graphics are translated to. This may fix some visual glitches on Apple GPUs, at the cost of speed.
help.Video@@Disable On-Disk Shader Cache: Stops loading shaders from, and saving them to, the shader cache on storage.
help.Video@@Disable Vertex Cache: Turns off the vertex cache. It may fix missing or flickering graphics, but can slow games down.
help.Video@@Disable Video Output: Turns off all video output and PS3 graphics rendering. Its only use is measuring CPU (Cell) performance during development.
help.Video@@Disable Vulkan Memory Allocator: Turns off the emulator's own Vulkan memory allocator and allocates GPU memory directly instead.
help.Video@@Disable ZCull Occlusion Queries: Skips occlusion queries for a small to moderate speed boost. It may break occlusion, causing missing geometry or heavy pop-in.
help.Video@@Emulate Special Depth Comparison: Emulates depth comparisons, usually EQUAL modes, where modern GPUs behave differently from the PS3. Fixes heavy shadow flicker and Z-fighting in some games.
help.Video@@Force CPU Blit: Does all image copy and scaling work on the CPU. It is more accurate in some cases but much slower, usually needs 'Write Color Buffers' on, and overrides 'GPU texture scaling'.
help.Video@@Force Hardware MSAA Resolve: Uses the GPU's own MSAA resolve for all sampling. It can give crisper visuals with MSAA on, but costs speed and may cause visual artifacts.
help.Video@@Force High Precision Z buffer: Uses a high precision depth (Z) buffer, which is only useful when debugging differences between GPUs. If unsure, leave it off.
help.Video@@Frame limit: Off is fastest, but some games crash if the frame rate runs too high. Use PS3 native only if Auto does not work right, since it can cause uneven frame pacing.
help.Video@@Framebuffer Aliasing Heuristic Bi: Decides how render targets are handled when color and depth share memory. Auto suits most games; Prefer Color fixes missing geometry in a few, but skips the depth test for that draw.
help.Video@@Handle RSX Memory Tiling: Follows the PS3's memory tiling layout when writing GPU data back to memory. It can fix graphics corruption seen with Read Color or Read Depth on.
help.Video@@Log shader programs: Saves the game's shaders to files. Only useful to developers; if unsure, leave it off.
help.Video@@MSAA: Emulates the PS3's multisampling layout. It can fix some hard-to-solve graphics glitches, with a low to moderate speed cost depending on the GPU.
help.Video@@Multithreaded RSX: Moves some graphics work to a second thread. It helps on CPUs with many cores, but can slow down weaker ones.
help.Video@@Output Scaling Mode: Nearest applies no filtering, Bilinear smooths the image, and FidelityFX Super Resolution upscales it when the game renders below screen resolution. FidelityFX can cause artifacts and skips stereo 3D.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Center Horiz: Centers the performance overlay horizontally, ignoring the horizontal margin.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Center Verti: Centers the performance overlay vertically, ignoring the vertical margin.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Detail level: Sets how much information the performance overlay shows.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Enable Frame: Shows a frame rate graph in the performance overlay.
Shows a frame time graph in the performance overlay.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Position: Sets which corner of the screen the performance overlay appears in.
help.Video@@Performance Overlay@@Use Window S: Places the overlay against the whole screen instead of the game's picture, so it can sit outside the game area.
help.Video@@Read Color Buffers: Fills color render targets with data from the emulated PS3 memory.
help.Video@@Read Depth Buffer: Fills depth render targets with data from the emulated PS3 memory.
help.Video@@Record With Overlays: Includes the emulator's overlays in recordings and screenshots.
help.Video@@Renderdoc Compatibility Mode: Adds Vulkan debug markers so graphics capture tools give clearer captures. If unsure, leave it off.
help.Video@@Renderer: Chooses the graphics renderer. Leave it on Vulkan, the only renderer available on iPhone and iPad.
help.Video@@Resolution: Leave this on 1280x720, which every PS3 game supports, and use 1920x1080 only if the game supports it. It is ignored when Resolution Scale is not 100%.
help.Video@@Shader Compiler Threads: Sets how many threads compile shaders. It only matters when the shader mode is one of the asynchronous modes.
help.Video@@Shader Loading Dialog@@Allow cust: Shows a background image on the shader loading screen. By default it is the game's own PIC1.PNG artwork.
help.Video@@Shader Loading Dialog@@Blur effec: Sets how strongly the shader loading screen's background image is blurred, for readability or looks.
help.Video@@Shader Loading Dialog@@Darkening: Sets how much the shader loading screen's background image is darkened, for readability or looks.
help.Video@@Shader Precision: Sets how precise generated shaders are. Low precision can run much faster on some hardware, but may cause minor visual glitches or flicker.
help.Video@@Stretch To Display Area: Ignores the aspect ratio and stretches the picture to fill the screen.
help.Video@@Strict Rendering Mode: Follows the graphics API specification strictly. It can fix rare missing graphics and flicker but may slow some games; if unsure, leave it off.
help.Video@@Strict Texture Flushing: Flushes textures even when it is not needed. It is known to cause visual artifacts, but helps debug certain texture cache problems.
help.Video@@Use GPU texture scaling: Does all texture transfers, scaling and conversion on the GPU. It may corrupt textures in some cases.
help.Video@@VSync Mode: Syncs frames to the screen to stop tearing. Adaptive mode keeps the frame rate up but may skip frames or tear; Full mode never tears and caps the frame rate at the screen's refresh rate.
help.Video@@Vulkan@@Asynchronous Queue Schedu: Sets how GPU compute jobs are scheduled for asynchronous texture streaming. 'Safe' follows the spec and works on all devices at some CPU cost; 'Fast' is quicker but hacky.
help.Video@@Vulkan@@Asynchronous Texture Stre: Uploads textures to the GPU alongside 3D rendering using async compute. It can help on powerful GPUs with spare headroom, and works best with Multithreaded RSX on.
help.Video@@Vulkan@@Use Re-BAR for GPU upload: Uploads timing-sensitive data straight into GPU memory the CPU can write to (resizable BAR). In games with very high frame rates it can lower performance.
help.Video@@Write Color Buffers: Turn this on if graphics are missing or lighting looks broken. It may slow some games or cause stutter, and Demon's Souls needs it.
help.Video@@Write Depth Buffer: Writes depth buffer values back to the emulated PS3 memory.
